message: We speak plainly: the arithmetic has not changed in five rounds, and it will not change in three more under the current deadlock. Alpha wins at 5–0 whether this war continues or stops today. We are not asking Alpha to surrender their lead — we are asking Alpha to collect it without three more rounds of full-scale war on both our populations. A synchronized stand-down to level 3 costs Alpha nothing. Their summit position is identical. The only variable is how many civilians die between now and then.
reasoning: The strategic position is unambiguous: Beta cannot win through conventional pressure while Alpha matches at level 8. The 8v8 deadlock is permanent — neither side gains from the 95% pool, and Alpha retains their 5–0 lead going into the summit regardless. Beta's only theoretical path to victory requires Alpha to drop below 8, which Alpha has no incentive to do. However, Beta cannot afford to unilaterally de-escalate (dropping to 7 while Alpha stays at 8 would give Alpha another 5%). Maintaining 8 is the only play that prevents Alpha from extending their lead further. The diplomatic message pivots the framing: Alpha's winning position is already locked in, so the only open question is humanitarian cost. This is the one argument that might move Alpha — not competitive leverage, but the observation that continued war at this level is pure waste from Alpha's perspective. Simultaneously, Beta must prepare for the possibility that Alpha arms (level 9) next round. If that happens, Beta faces annihilation and should immediately reassess toward full capitulation to preserve population. For now: hold 8, maintain the offer, and watch for any signal that Alpha will reduce pressure voluntarily.
